stem: A retailer is designing a new workload and wants explicit architectural guidance on lowering the energy consumption and environmental impact of the resources it runs. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar addresses that goal?

options.text: Reliability, which covers performing an intended function correctly and consistently
Sustainability, which focuses on environmental impact and energy efficiency
Cost optimization, which covers delivering business value at the lowest price point
Operational excellence, which focuses on building software correctly and delivering a great customer experience

explanation: Sustainability is the Well-Architected pillar defined around environmental impacts, especially energy consumption and efficiency as the levers an architect can act on. The other options target workload correctness, spend, and software delivery rather than environmental footprint.

distractorNotes.a: Reliability is about a workload performing its intended function correctly and consistently, not about energy use.
distractorNotes.c: Cost optimization targets the lowest price point for business value, which is a financial rather than environmental goal.
distractorNotes.d: Operational excellence focuses on building software correctly and delivering a great customer experience, not environmental impact.

stem: During a large migration, one legacy application will move to AWS with no changes made to the application itself. A second application will move to AWS with its self-managed SQL Server database switched to Amazon RDS for SQL Server. Which TWO of the 7 Rs migration strategies do these two plans use? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Retire, which decommissions an application rather than moving it at all
Rehost, also called lift and shift, which moves an application unchanged
Repurchase, which replaces the application with a different product
Replatform, which moves an application and applies some optimization
Refactor, which re-architects an application around cloud-native features

explanation: AWS documents seven migration strategies, the 7 Rs. Rehost is described as lift and shift: the application moves from the source environment to AWS without any changes, which matches the first application. Replatform is described as lift, tinker, and shift: the application moves with some optimization applied, and AWS gives replatforming a SQL Server database to Amazon RDS for SQL Server as the example, which matches the second application.

distractorNotes.a: Retire applies to applications you decommission or archive instead of migrating.
distractorNotes.c: Repurchase, or drop and shop, means replacing the application with a different product such as a SaaS offering.
distractorNotes.e: Refactor means modifying the architecture to use cloud-native features, which is more than the described change.

sourceNote: AWS Prescriptive Guidance - the 7 Rs migration strategies, rehost and replatform

stem: A company currently buys and racks servers years in advance to cover projected peak demand. After it moves those workloads to AWS, how does its infrastructure spending model primarily change?

options.text: Fixed upfront expense becomes variable expense, paying only for what it uses
The same fixed capital purchase cycle continues, but AWS installs the hardware
One flat annual platform fee is charged that covers unlimited AWS consumption
Infrastructure spending disappears entirely because AWS absorbs the compute cost

explanation: AWS describes trading fixed expense for variable expense as a core advantage of cloud computing: instead of investing heavily in data centers and servers before knowing how they will be used, you pay only when you consume computing resources and only for how much you consume. Capacity no longer has to be bought ahead of demand.

distractorNotes.b: The point of the change is that the upfront capital purchase cycle goes away, not that AWS performs it for you.
distractorNotes.c: AWS consumption is metered per use; there is no flat all-you-can-use annual platform fee.
distractorNotes.d: Spending does not disappear; it shifts from upfront capital purchases to metered consumption charges.

sourceNote: Six advantages of cloud computing - trade fixed expense for variable expense

stem: A media company cannot predict traffic for an upcoming launch and does not want to buy capacity for a peak that may never happen. Which AWS Well-Architected general design principle does running this workload on AWS let the team apply?

options.text: Improve through game days, by simulating production events on a schedule
Drive architectures using data gathered about how the workload behaves
Stop guessing capacity needs, scaling in and out automatically as required
Test systems at production scale using a full-size environment on demand

explanation: Stop guessing your capacity needs is a general design principle of the Well-Architected Framework. AWS notes that a poor capacity decision leaves you either with expensive idle resources or with the performance consequences of too little capacity, and that in the cloud you can use as much or as little capacity as you need and scale in and out automatically. That directly answers unpredictable launch traffic.

distractorNotes.a: Game days are scheduled simulations of production events to test architecture and processes, not a response to unknown demand.
distractorNotes.b: Driving architectures using data is about collecting evidence to improve design choices over time.
distractorNotes.d: Testing at production scale is about creating and then decommissioning a full-size test environment, not about sizing live capacity.

sourceNote: Well-Architected Framework - general design principle: stop guessing your capacity needs

stem: A company runs a web application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, who is responsible for applying operating system updates and security patches to that instance's guest operating system?

options.text: AWS, because it manages the hypervisor and therefore every layer above it
AWS, because patching is bundled into the hourly price of every instance
Neither party, because EC2 guest operating systems patch themselves in place
The customer, because guest operating system management is a customer duty

explanation: AWS categorizes Amazon EC2 as infrastructure as a service, so the customer performs the security configuration and management tasks above the hypervisor. AWS states that customers who deploy an EC2 instance are responsible for management of the guest operating system, including updates and security patches, plus any application software they install and the configuration of the AWS-provided security group.

distractorNotes.a: AWS responsibility stops at the virtualization layer for EC2; the guest operating system sits on the customer side of the boundary.
distractorNotes.b: Instance pricing covers the underlying infrastructure, not guest operating system patching, which the customer performs.
distractorNotes.c: EC2 does not automatically patch customer guest operating systems; the customer must manage that work.

sourceNote: AWS shared responsibility model - EC2 customers manage the guest OS including updates and security patches

stem: An engineer holds full IAM administrator permissions in a standalone AWS account that is not part of AWS Organizations. Which task still requires signing in with the account root user credentials?

options.text: Creating an IAM role that grants an application read access to Amazon S3 buckets
Closing the standalone AWS account
Enabling Amazon GuardDuty threat detection across the whole account
Attaching a customer managed policy to an existing IAM user group

explanation: AWS publishes a specific list of tasks that can be performed only by the account root user. For a standalone account that is not part of AWS Organizations, closing the account requires root user credentials. Everyday administrative work such as creating roles, attaching policies, or turning on security services can be delegated to an IAM principal with the right permissions.

distractorNotes.a: Creating IAM roles is ordinary IAM administration and does not appear on the root-only task list.
distractorNotes.c: Enabling GuardDuty can be done by any principal with the necessary service permissions.
distractorNotes.d: Attaching managed policies to groups is standard IAM administration available to a permitted IAM principal.

sourceNote: IAM User Guide - tasks that require root user credentials, including closing a standalone AWS account

stem: A startup has just created its first AWS account and wants to protect the account root user. Which TWO actions match the AWS root user best practices? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Enable multi-factor authentication for root user sign-in
Create root user access keys so deployment scripts can run
Use a company group email address for the root user account
Share the root user password with the whole platform team
Sign in as the root user to do routine daily administration

explanation: AWS advises adding MFA to the root user because the root user can perform privileged actions, and it recommends a business-managed group email address that forwards to several people so AWS can always reach an account owner. AWS separately recommends against creating root access keys, against sharing root credentials, and against using the root user for everyday work.

distractorNotes.b: AWS strongly recommends not creating access keys for the root user, and suggests console sign-in or temporary credentials instead.
distractorNotes.d: AWS says not to share the root user password, MFA, or access keys except with people who have a strict business need.
distractorNotes.e: AWS recommends creating an administrative user for everyday tasks and reserving the root user for tasks that require it.

sourceNote: IAM User Guide - root user best practices: enable MFA, use a group email, avoid root access keys

stem: An external auditor asks a company to supply AWS SOC and PCI compliance reports covering the AWS infrastructure that the company's workloads run on. Where should the company obtain those reports?

options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor, by exporting the results of its security checks
Amazon Inspector, by running a compliance scan across the account
AWS Artifact, by downloading the on-demand compliance documents
AWS Config, by generating a resource configuration history report

explanation: AWS Artifact provides on-demand downloads of AWS security and compliance documents, explicitly including ISO and PCI reports and System and Organization Controls (SOC) reports, plus certifications from accreditation bodies. Those documents can be handed to auditors or regulators as audit artifacts, and AWS provides them free of charge.

distractorNotes.a: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks on your own resources, not AWS third-party audit reports.
distractorNotes.b: Amazon Inspector assesses workloads for vulnerabilities; it does not publish AWS audit reports.
distractorNotes.d: AWS Config records how your resources are configured over time, which is not an AWS compliance attestation.

sourceNote: What is AWS Artifact - on-demand downloads of AWS SOC, PCI, and ISO compliance documents

stem: A security team wants a service that continuously analyzes AWS CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs, and DNS logs to surface findings such as compromised credentials or unauthorized cryptomining on EC2 instances. Which service does this?

options.text: Amazon GuardDuty, a threat detection service that monitors those data sources
AWS WAF, which filters inbound web requests against configurable rule sets
AWS Artifact, which supplies on-demand AWS compliance documentation
Amazon Inspector, which scans workloads for software vulnerabilities

explanation: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously monitors and analyzes AWS data sources and logs. Its foundational data sources are CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs, and DNS logs, which it ingests automatically when GuardDuty is enabled. AWS lists compromised and exfiltrated credentials and unauthorized cryptomining on EC2 instances among the threats it detects.

distractorNotes.b: AWS WAF inspects and filters web requests to protected applications; it is not a log-analysis threat detection service.
distractorNotes.c: AWS Artifact is a document portal for AWS audit reports and agreements, with no detection capability.
distractorNotes.d: Amazon Inspector performs vulnerability assessment of workloads rather than continuous log-based threat detection.

sourceNote: What is Amazon GuardDuty - foundational data sources and detected threat scenarios

stem: An Amazon S3 bucket is deleted unexpectedly. An investigator needs to establish which identity made the deletion API call and at what time. Which AWS service records that information?

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch, which collects operational metrics and log data
VPC Flow Logs, which capture IP traffic to and from network interfaces
AWS Config, which records how resources are configured over time
AWS CloudTrail, which records actions taken by users, roles, and services

explanation: AWS CloudTrail enables operational and risk auditing, governance, and compliance for an AWS account. Actions taken by a user, a role, or an AWS service are recorded as CloudTrail events, covering the console, the AWS CLI, and the SDKs and APIs. AWS states that CloudTrail lets you identify who or what took which action, what resources were acted upon, and when the event occurred.

distractorNotes.a: CloudWatch focuses on metrics, logs, and alarms for operational monitoring rather than an attributable API call record.
distractorNotes.b: VPC Flow Logs record network traffic metadata, not the identity behind an AWS API call.
distractorNotes.c: AWS Config tracks resource configuration state and compliance over time, not the caller identity and timing of each API action.

sourceNote: What is AWS CloudTrail - records who took which action, on what resource, and when

stem: A team is deciding where to place a production workload on AWS. Which TWO statements about AWS Regions and Availability Zones are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An Availability Zone spans several AWS Regions on the same continent
AWS automatically replicates your resources into every other Region
Each AWS Region contains multiple, isolated Availability Zones
An AWS Region is always made up of exactly one Availability Zone
Spreading instances across Availability Zones survives one location failing

explanation: AWS documents that each Region has multiple, isolated locations known as Availability Zones, identified by the Region code plus a letter such as us-east-1a. It also states that launching instances in multiple Availability Zones protects applications from the failure of a single location within the Region.

distractorNotes.a: The containment runs the other way: Availability Zones sit inside a single Region, not across Regions.
distractorNotes.b: AWS states that Regions are isolated from each other and that resources are not automatically replicated across Regions.
distractorNotes.d: A Region contains multiple Availability Zones, which is what makes multi-zone resilience possible.

sourceNote: EC2 Regions and Zones - Regions contain multiple isolated AZs; multi-AZ protects against single-location failure

stem: A hospital must retain medical imaging archives in Amazon S3 for seven years. The data is expected to be accessed less than once a year, and a retrieval time of up to 48 hours is acceptable. Which S3 storage class gives the lowest storage cost?

options.text: S3 Standard-IA, for long-lived data that still needs millisecond access
S3 Glacier Deep Archive, the lowest-cost class for yearly access
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, for quarterly access in milliseconds
S3 Standard, the default class for frequently accessed objects

explanation: AWS recommends S3 Glacier Deep Archive for archive data accessed less than once a year, describes it as designed for retaining data sets for multiple years to meet compliance requirements, and calls it the lowest-cost storage option in AWS. Its bulk retrieval tier typically restores objects within 48 hours, which fits the stated tolerance, and its 180-day minimum duration is comfortably inside a seven-year retention period.

distractorNotes.a: S3 Standard-IA targets infrequently accessed data that still needs millisecond retrieval, so it costs more to store than Deep Archive.
distractorNotes.c: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is sized for roughly quarterly access with millisecond retrieval, and stores at a higher cost than Deep Archive.
distractorNotes.d: S3 Standard is the default class for frequently accessed data and is the most expensive of these options to store long-term archives.

sourceNote: S3 Glacier storage classes - Deep Archive for less-than-annual access, lowest-cost option, bulk retrieval within 48 hours

stem: A team wants to run two workloads without provisioning or managing any servers: a piece of event-driven application code, and a set of containers. Which TWO AWS compute services are serverless options for this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Amazon EC2, which provides resizable virtual server capacity
AWS Lambda, which runs code without provisioning servers
Amazon Lightsail, which bundles a virtual server with storage
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, which adjusts instance capacity
AWS Fargate, which is serverless compute for containers

explanation: AWS groups AWS Lambda under the serverless compute category and describes it as running code without thinking about servers, paying only for the compute time consumed. AWS Fargate is listed in the container category and described as serverless compute for containers. Together they cover event-driven code and containers with no servers to provision or manage.

distractorNotes.a: Amazon EC2 provides virtual servers, which you size, launch, and maintain yourself.
distractorNotes.c: Amazon Lightsail packages a virtual server with storage and networking, so servers are still part of the model.
distractorNotes.d: EC2 Auto Scaling adds and removes EC2 capacity in response to demand, but the underlying instances are still servers.

sourceNote: AWS Overview compute services - Lambda listed as serverless, Fargate as serverless compute for containers

stem: A read-heavy web application repeatedly issues the same expensive queries against its relational database. The team wants to serve those repeated reads from an in-memory cache at microsecond latency. Which AWS service fits that role?

options.text: Amazon RDS, a managed relational database for transactional workloads
Amazon Redshift, a data warehouse for large-scale analytics queries
Amazon ElastiCache, in-memory caching at microsecond latency
Amazon DynamoDB, a key-value store with millisecond read performance

explanation: AWS maps the in-memory database category to caching, session management, and similar use cases, and lists Amazon ElastiCache as the service that unlocks microsecond latency with in-memory caching. AWS also describes ElastiCache as improving web application performance by retrieving information from fast managed in-memory caches instead of relying entirely on slower disk-based databases.

distractorNotes.a: Amazon RDS is the relational database being cached in this scenario, not the cache in front of it.
distractorNotes.b: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics, not a low-latency cache for application reads.
distractorNotes.d: AWS positions DynamoDB as a key-value database delivering single-digit millisecond performance, not microsecond in-memory caching.

sourceNote: AWS Overview databases - in-memory category maps caching use cases to ElastiCache at microsecond latency

stem: An engineer adds an inbound rule to a security group so that clients can reach an EC2 instance over HTTPS. Does a matching outbound rule also have to be added before the instance's replies can reach those clients?

options.text: No, because security groups are stateful and return traffic is allowed automatically
Yes, because a security group evaluates its inbound and outbound rules separately
Yes, because return traffic needs an explicit outbound allow rule to be permitted
No, because the subnet's network ACL always permits replies from any instance

explanation: AWS documents that security groups are stateful: return traffic is automatically allowed, regardless of any outbound rule. That is the documented difference from network ACLs, which are stateless and require return traffic to be explicitly allowed. Security groups also operate at the instance level and support allow rules only.

distractorNotes.b: Because security groups are stateful, the response to an allowed inbound flow is permitted without a separate outbound rule.
distractorNotes.c: Explicitly allowing return traffic is the requirement for stateless network ACLs, not for security groups.
distractorNotes.d: Network ACLs are stateless and can contain deny rules, so they do not blanket-permit replies from any instance.

sourceNote: Amazon VPC - security group versus network ACL comparison, return traffic automatically allowed (stateful)

stem: An order service must hand work to a processing component without losing messages while that component is unavailable. Separately, each new order event must be pushed to many subscriber endpoints at once for parallel processing. Which TWO services meet these needs? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Amazon SQS, a managed queue that stores messages until consumers read them
Amazon CloudFront, a content delivery network that caches data at edge sites
AWS Direct Connect, a dedicated private link from a data center into AWS
Amazon SNS, a pub/sub service that fans messages out to many subscribers
Amazon Route 53, a managed DNS service that also registers domain names

explanation: AWS describes Amazon SQS as a fully managed message queuing service that lets you send, store, and receive messages between software components at any volume without losing messages or requiring other services to be available, which covers the durable hand-off. AWS describes Amazon SNS as a pub/sub service whose topics let publishers fan out messages to a large number of subscriber endpoints for parallel processing, which covers the broadcast requirement.

distractorNotes.b: CloudFront is a content delivery network for caching and serving content, not an application messaging service.
distractorNotes.c: Direct Connect provides dedicated private network connectivity into AWS and does not carry application messages between components.
distractorNotes.e: Route 53 handles DNS resolution and domain registration rather than message queuing or publish and subscribe delivery.

sourceNote: AWS Overview application integration - SQS message queuing without losing messages; SNS topics fan out to many subscribers

stem: A company runs a batch analytics job that has flexible start times and tolerates being interrupted. Separately, it has a steady baseline of compute usage that it is willing to commit to in dollars per hour for a one-year term. Which TWO purchasing options best fit these two cases? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Dedicated Hosts, physical servers dedicated to a single customer
On-Demand Instances, billed by the second with no commitment
Spot Instances, unused EC2 capacity at a significant discount
Savings Plans, a commitment to hourly spend over one or three years
Capacity Reservations, reserved capacity in one Availability Zone

explanation: AWS states that Spot Instances request unused EC2 capacity and are a cost-effective choice when you can be flexible about when applications run and they can be interrupted, which matches the batch job. AWS describes Savings Plans as reducing EC2 costs through a commitment to a consistent amount of usage measured in USD per hour for a one-year or three-year term, which matches the steady baseline.

distractorNotes.a: Dedicated Hosts address single-tenant hardware and license-bound software, not interruptible batch work or spend commitments.
distractorNotes.b: On-Demand carries no commitment and no discount, so it fits neither the interruptible job nor the committed baseline.
distractorNotes.e: Capacity Reservations hold capacity in a specific Availability Zone; they are about capacity assurance rather than a usage spend commitment.

sourceNote: EC2 billing and purchasing options - Spot for interruptible flexible workloads; Savings Plans commit to USD/hour for 1 or 3 years

stem: A finance team wants to be notified automatically whenever AWS cost or usage crosses a spending threshold that the team defines for the month. Which AWS Billing and Cost Management feature should they configure?

options.text: AWS Cost Explorer, which visualizes and analyzes cost and usage data
AWS Pricing Calculator, which estimates the cost of a planned workload
Cost allocation tags, which group charges by team or by environment
AWS Budgets, which alerts when costs exceed a defined threshold

explanation: AWS lists Budgets under budgeting and planning, describing it as setting custom budgets for cost and usage to govern costs across the organization and receiving alerts when costs exceed defined thresholds. The other features analyze, estimate, or organize costs, but they are not the mechanism that raises a threshold alert.

distractorNotes.a: Cost Explorer analyzes and forecasts cost and usage with visuals, filtering, and grouping, rather than firing threshold alerts.
distractorNotes.b: Pricing Calculator produces estimates for planned workloads before the spend happens.
distractorNotes.c: Cost allocation tags organize charges into dimensions for reporting; they do not raise alerts on their own.

sourceNote: AWS Billing and Cost Management - Budgets sets custom cost/usage budgets and alerts when thresholds are exceeded
